### New

- **Minecraft 1.21.1, 1.21.4 and 1.21.5.** There are now jars for Minecraft 1.21.1, 1.21.4 and 1.21.5 too, next to 1.21.6 to 1.21.8, 1.21.10, 1.21.11, 26.1, 26.2 and 26.3.
- **View lock.** A new setting under **Lyrics → Position**, and a key you can set in Controls ("Lock lyrics here"): it pins the lyrics where you are looking right now, so they stay put while you look around. Press the key again to let them follow as before. In World, new words gather round the spot you locked.
- **Show underground too.** A new setting under **Display → Hide lyrics**: the lyrics stay visible in caves and under roofs, instead of hiding when there is no open sky above you.
- **Recently heard.** The song library now has a **Recently heard** list of the songs you played, so it works without Spotify too. It is kept on this computer only, and **Forget recently heard** empties it.
- **Card lines.** A new option under **Display → Record card**: the card can show the line before and the line after the one being sung, dimmed, around it. The card grows to fit and still keeps clear of your hotbar.
- **Settings with the keyboard.** The whole settings screen now works without a mouse: Tab or the arrow keys move from row to row, left and right change a choice or slider, Enter or Space switches it, Page Up and Page Down scroll, Ctrl+Tab changes tabs and Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) searches. With the Narrator on, each row reads out its name, its value and its place in the list (like "Layout, choice, Arc, 1 of 3"), and the song library reads out the song you are on, the section, the buttons and the search box.

### Updating from 0.7.8

- Your settings, saved lyrics, album covers, Spotify sign-in and key bindings carry over.
- This one update is still installed by 0.7.8's own updater. If your mods folder is a link to another folder, or (on Windows) the folder your game lives in has accented letters, 0.7.8 can't install it by itself: download the new jar and replace the old one by hand this once. From 0.7.9 on, the mod handles both.

### Better looking

- **Settings fit small screens.** On a small window or a big GUI scale, a row with a wide control (like the colour swatches or a long list of choices) now puts the control on its own line under its name, instead of hiding the name or cutting its description short (like "Colour" on the Look tab, which showed only "From t…"). Long titles no longer run into the buttons at the top.
- **Easier to read grey text.** The dim grey used for artists, hints and subtitles is a little brighter.

### Faster

- **Night skies cost less when you look away.** Parts of the Galaxy, Comet, Eclipse, Synthwave and Moonlight skies (and their moon, sun, stars and glow) that are behind you or off the screen aren't drawn.
- **The game starts a little faster.** Some parts of the mod are now made ready the first time they are needed, not while the game loads.
- **Lyrics cost less when you look away from them.** Lines that are well off screen aren't drawn, glow and all.
- **Light mode is lighter.** With **Display → Performance → Effects** set to Light, World words skip their dark outline (they keep their shadow).

### Fixed

- **The Record card keeps off your off-hand slot.** In a bottom corner at some window sizes, the card could sit on the item in your other hand, or on the attack indicator. Now it moves out of the way, for left- and right-handed players.
- **Song library.** On the Shelf view, pointing at a cover now shows its name before you click (a click plays it). Space plays the chosen song, and the sign-in and "Try again" buttons work from the keyboard.
- **The look picker reads right in Hebrew.** Its heading was drawn backwards.
- **World lyrics show on Minecraft 26.1.** On Minecraft 26.1, the World layout (the one you get at first) showed no words at all. Now it does.
- **Lyrics show again when LRCLIB is busy.** LRCLIB, the free lyrics site the mod uses, often answers "busy" to its quick exact lookup for songs it hasn't looked up lately, while its normal search still works. The mod gave up on that answer and said "Couldn't reach the lyrics sites", or fell back to the backup for no reason. Now it goes on to LRCLIB's search, so those songs get their lyrics. Thanks to the player who reported this and found the cause (GitHub issue #1).
- **Backup lyrics aren't kept for good.** When LRCLIB was down and the NetEase backup filled in, those lyrics were saved and used every time the song played, even after LRCLIB was back. Now they're only used while LRCLIB is down, and the next play asks LRCLIB again.
- **Old backup lyrics get a second look.** Lyrics saved from the backup site by 0.7.8 while LRCLIB was down are checked against LRCLIB once more, and replaced if it has them. You keep what you had until then.
- **Lyrics come back after a Wi-Fi login page.** On hotel or café Wi-Fi before you log in, or behind a proxy, the lyrics site's answer could be replaced by an empty page or a redirect. The mod then said "no lyrics" for that song for three days. Now it counts that as a failed try and asks again. A short timeout on the backup site no longer counts as "no lyrics" either.
- **Right lyrics for songs without an artist.** Browser audio often has no artist and no length. Then the mod took the first song on the lyrics site with a similar title, which could be another song's lyrics. Now the title has to match, and when different artists have a song with that title, it shows none rather than guess.
- **Skipping songs fast.** When the lyrics site was slow, the next song's lyrics, even ones already saved, waited for the old song's lookup to give up. Now the old lookup is dropped right away.
- **Lyrics that wouldn't load stay fixable.** A song whose saved lyrics couldn't be read stayed empty for good. Now it is looked up again after three days, like any song without lyrics. When the site asks the mod to slow down, it waits as long as asked. Songs whose lyrics are only music notes now show as instrumental.
- **The Hebrew Animation row fits.** In Hebrew, the label under the Animation setting was cut off. Now it fits.
- **No stray time stamps in lyrics.** Some lyric files have a time stamp in the middle or at the end of a line, and it showed up as text like "[00:14.00]". Now it's hidden.
- **Huge album covers are skipped.** A broken or oversized album cover could stall the game or run it out of memory. Covers over 8 MB, or wider or taller than 4096 pixels, are now skipped (real ones are far smaller), in the song library and for the song that is playing.
- **Auto-update with linked folders.** Some launchers link the mods or instance folder to somewhere else. Automatic updates silently never ran there. Now they do.
- **Chinese and Japanese songs keep all their lines.** Lyrics from the NetEase backup lost every sung line that started with a few characters and a colon, like 他说：我爱你 ("he said: I love you"), because the mod took them for songwriter credits. Now only real credit lines at the start and end of a song are left out.
- **A frozen music player doesn't freeze the lyrics.** On Linux, if one music player stopped answering (a stuck browser tab, say), the lyrics and every other player froze for many seconds at a time. Now the mod goes on with the players that answer.
- **The chosen player is followed properly.** When you pick a player (like mpv or Firefox) and it has several windows open, the mod now follows the one that is playing.
- **One song is one song.** Browsers often send a song's title a moment before its artist. That made the mod look up the lyrics twice, list the song twice under Recently heard and flash the top bar twice. Now it waits a moment for the artist.
- **Lyrics don't blink out.** A single failed or empty answer from your music player (Spotify too) cleared the lyrics and loaded them again. Now they stay; a real stop still clears them within about 2 seconds.
- **Faster or slower playback stays in sync.** Lyrics now keep time with a podcast or video played at 1.5x, 2x or another speed, on Linux players and on Windows players that report their speed.
- **Song detection can't stop for good.** A rare error while handling a song change could silently stop the mod from following your music until you restarted the game. Now it carries on.
- **You always hear about a new version.** With automatic updates on, a download that failed (a slow connection, say) meant you were told nothing at all. Now you still get the "new version available" message.
- **Updates on Windows with accented folder names.** On Windows, if the folder your game lives in has accented or non-English letters in its path (like C:\Users\José\AppData\Roaming\.minecraft), the automatic update could never finish and downloaded itself again on every start. Now the mod tells you a new version is out so you can install it yourself. When only your user folder has such letters and the game lives elsewhere (on D:\Games, say), the update now installs itself as usual.
- **Song detection on Windows with a ’ in the folder name.** If the folder your game lives in had a curly apostrophe in its name (like "Beli’s Pack"), the mod could not read what your music player was playing on Windows. Now it can.
- **Settings stay saved on Windows.** On Windows, antivirus, OneDrive or the search indexer often hold a file open for a moment, and then a settings change, a saved lyric or your Spotify sign-in was silently not saved. The mod now tries again for a moment. Saving also works on network drives and USB sticks that couldn't do it before.
- **One odd setting no longer resets all of them.** If your settings file had one value the mod couldn't read (a typo, or a value from another version), every setting went back to default, and the next change saved over the file. Now only that setting resets, and the old file is kept as skylyrics.json.bad. The Recently heard list is kept the same way (heard.json.bad), and one bad song in it no longer drops the rest.
- **No crash when skipping through songs fast.** Skipping several songs in quick succession could, rarely, crash the game or show the wrong album cover.
- **Signing out of Spotify or quitting doesn't freeze.** If Spotify was refreshing your sign-in at that moment, signing out or quitting the game could hang for several seconds.
- **Your Spotify sign-in stays private on shared Windows PCs.** When the game folder was outside your own user folder (on D:\Games, say), other accounts on the same PC could read your Spotify sign-in file. Now only your account can.
- **Spotify sign-in doesn't fail at random.** Browsers sometimes open a spare connection that stays silent, and that could make the Spotify sign-in give up with "Sign-in timed out". Now it keeps waiting for the real answer. If the sign-in can't start because another game is signing in at the same moment, you get a clear message instead of a technical one.
- **Updates are checked more carefully.** A downloaded update is only used when it really is Beli's SkyLyrics, in the version that was expected. It is only ever downloaded from the mod's own GitHub releases, and a download over 20 MB is refused.
- **Flashes with each new line work in the World layout.** The crosshair flash, "Pulse with the lyrics" for the sky and the hat glow never fired in the World layout, the one you get at first. They only worked in Arc and Lines. Now they flash with every new line in every layout.
- **Cmd shortcuts on a Mac.** In the settings and library searches, Cmd+F and Cmd+Backspace now work. Before, they needed the Ctrl key.
- **Less work on a Mac.** If you said no when macOS asked to let Minecraft control Spotify or Music, the mod asked the system again about once a second, forever. Now it waits a while between tries, and the other app keeps working. The mod also checks which music apps are open less often.
- **Accented song names on a Mac.** Songs with accents from older Music libraries (like "Café") now find their lyrics.
- **Works next to other crosshair mods.** If another mod changes how the crosshair is drawn, the game no longer refuses to start because of SkyLyrics. At worst, SkyLyrics' crosshair styles don't show.
- **Album covers come back.** A cover that failed to download, after a short network hiccup say, is tried again after two minutes instead of staying blank for the rest of the session.
- **Exordium.** Exordium redraws the screen overlay less often, which can make the lyrics trail behind when you turn. The game log now says so, and the troubleshooting page explains how to fix it.
- **Clearer messages when something is wrong.** Music player errors now say what's wrong in plain words instead of Java error names like "IOException", and long messages are no longer cut off. On Windows, they say what to check. On Linux, if the game can't reach your music players, it tells you how to fix it, including the command a Flatpak Minecraft needs. "No lyrics" and "can't reach the lyrics sites" now say to press Retry or check your internet.
- **Lyrics for songs with a guest artist.** A "feat." in the song title was only left out of the lyrics search when it sat in plain brackets. Now it is also left out in Chinese and Japanese brackets like （feat. X） and 【feat. X】, and at the end of a title like "Song feat. X" or "Song ft. X", so those songs find their lyrics more often.
- **Emoji aren't cut in half.** When a long song title, artist or search text was shortened with "…", an emoji, a flag or an accented letter at the cut could turn into a broken symbol. Now the cut always falls between whole characters, in the library and the settings too, and a song without an album cover shows its first whole letter or emoji.
- **Aurora + nebula on Minecraft 26.2 and 26.3.** With the "Aurora + nebula" night sky, the nebula clouds showed as dark, solid shapes that cut the aurora off when you looked up. Now the aurora shines through them as it does on the other versions.
- **Arabic words keep all their letters.** In the World layout, Arabic words with joined letters (like لا) or vowel marks lost their last letters, so "سلام" showed without its م. Now every letter shows.
- **Hebrew and Arabic read the right way round.** In the World, Lines and Arc layouts, a word or a wrapped row of a Hebrew or Arabic line that started with English letters or a number was laid out as if the line read left to right. Now it keeps the line's direction.
- **Commas stay with Hebrew words in English lines.** In a line that starts in English, like "hello שלום,", the comma after a Hebrew word was drawn on its left. Now it stays on its right, where it is read, in the World and Lines layouts and in the top bar.
- **Long Arabic lines fill in step.** In the Lines layout, a long Arabic line that wraps onto a second row filled in (karaoke, typewriter) ahead of the singing on that row. Now each row fills as it is sung. Any line that wraps onto more rows also stays in step now: before, each new row's karaoke fill lagged a letter behind.
- **Lyrics without timing in the World layout.** For songs whose lyrics have no timing, the World layout showed only the last two words of each line, and the last line never went away. Now the words come out one by one along each line, and the last line leaves.
- **Lyrics with a translation on each line.** Some lyric files give a line and its translation (or its romanization) the same time, and only the second one ever showed. Now they show together, as "line / translation", in every layout. A broken file that puts many lines on one time is still shown line by line.
- **Very long words fit.** In the World layout, one very long word (a long "aaaaah" written out, say) could stretch across the whole view and hide the other words. Now it is shrunk to fit.
- **The Windows music reader stays calm.** When Windows' media service was broken, the mod started its music reader again every few seconds, using the processor each time. Now it waits 15 seconds between tries, and its messages are in your language (English and Hebrew).
- **The same music app is followed on Windows.** With two players going, closing one (a browser tab, say) could make the lyrics jump to the other one's song. Now they keep following the same app.
- **Slow first start on Windows.** With some antivirus programs, the Windows music reader took so long to start the first time that it never worked. It now gets more time on its first start.
- **Less memory on the title screen.** After you left a world, the mod kept that whole world in memory until you joined the next one. Now it lets go of it.
- **The song title shows once.** In the World layout, the song's title floated up again every time you went through a portal. Now it shows when the song starts or when you join a world.
- **No old cover after a quick skip.** Skipping fast from a song with an album cover to one without could leave the old cover showing. Now it goes.
- **No old colour tint after a quick skip.** Skipping at just the wrong moment could leave the previous song's cover colour tinting the next song. Not any more.
- **Changing the PC clock doesn't stop the lyrics site.** If your PC's clock jumped back (a time sync, say) just after the lyrics site failed once, the mod could skip that site for as long as the jump. Now it only skips it for the short wait it means to.
- **The Arc layout fades in again.** Switching from Arc to another layout and back made the line jump into its old place. Now it fades in like a new line.
- **No flash when lyrics come back.** Turning the lyrics off and on again in the middle of a song made the line from before you turned them off flash up for a moment. Not any more.
- **No old lyrics at a song change.** Right as a new song started, the old song's lyrics could show for a moment. Not any more.
- **Hats sit on top of helmets.** With a helmet, a carved pumpkin or a mob head on, several hats (the top hat, the propeller cap, the flower crown, the shades, the headphones, the straw cone and the pumpkin) sank into it or flickered. Now the hat grows just enough to sit outside it.
- **The antennae don't twitch.** The antennae hat jumped a little about every half minute. Now it sways smoothly.
- **Mixed Hebrew and English in the top bar.** A top bar line with both Hebrew and English words (like "שלום world 5") was mirrored as a whole, so the English words and numbers came out backwards. Now every word sits where it is read.
- **Chinese and Japanese in the top bar.** A Chinese or Japanese line counted as one long word, so the top bar jumped straight to its end and lit it all at once. Now it follows the singing character by character.
- **Even gaps between Arabic words in the top bar.** Arabic words were measured before their letters were joined, so the gaps between them came out uneven. Now they are measured as they are drawn.
- **Chinese and Japanese in the Arc and Lines layouts.** In the Arc layout, a long Chinese or Japanese line counted as one word, so it never wrapped and ran off the arc. Now it wraps into rows and comes in character by character, and a row may end after 。，、！？ or Arabic ، ؟ as it does after a comma. In the Lines layout, the Words animation and Grow word now work character by character too, instead of on the whole row.
- **Thai and very long words wrap.** In the Lines layout, Thai lyrics (which have no spaces between words) and one very long word ran past the edge. Now they wrap inside the line.
- **Odd song titles look normal.** A title with a stray line break, tab or hidden text-direction mark from the music player showed boxes or turned the title around. Now it shows as one clean line.
- **Seeking back in the World layout.** Jumping back in a song, or a song restarting or looping, left the words of lines that hadn't been sung yet hanging in the world. Now they leave, and the line being sung places its words again.

### Checked in game

- **Seen in game on Minecraft 1.21.11 (third batch):**
  - the aurora, nebula, Galaxy, Comet, Synthwave, Eclipse and Moonlight skies stay whole while you turn, with nothing popping in at the screen edges, also at a narrow field of view; the aurora looks as before
  - the settings work fully from the keyboard, including Ctrl+F search
  - the Record card keeps clear of the off-hand slot for left-handed players too (GUI scale 2)
  - the Hebrew Animation label fits
  - the frame rate is fine
  - the flash with each new line now shows in the World layout: frame by frame, the crosshair brightens for a moment just after the line changes and eases back, and the sky brightens a little with it
  - the Slide animation (the old line slides off one side as the new one comes in from the other) and the Blow animation (a leaving word drifts to the left as it fades)
  - the Dot, Cross, Circle and Corners crosshairs, and the normal one when it is picked
  - the rounded corners of the top bar, the Record card, the settings and the song library
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 1.21.1 (third batch, final build):** it starts and shows lyrics in the World and Arc layouts, the settings and a crosshair style.
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 26.3 and 26.2 (and again on 26.3 with the final build):** "Aurora + nebula" looks soft, with the aurora showing through the nebula, looking up, to the side and straight up; Nebula alone and Aurora alone look as before, and 26.1.2 is unchanged.
- **Seen working in game (on the hidden test screen):** World lyrics on Minecraft 26.1 by day and night; the Arc layout on 26.1; Minecraft 1.21.5 starts and shows lyrics, the top bar, the settings, the song library, a hat and a crosshair; View lock in Arc and World; Show underground too (lyrics stay under a big stone roof, hidden with it off); the Recently heard library with a song from mpv; on Minecraft 26.3 all 13 hats are lit right by day and night and the lyrics come back after you respawn.
- **Also seen in game:** Minecraft 1.21.4 starts and shows lyrics, the top bar, the settings, the library, a hat and a crosshair; the Record card keeps clear of the off-hand slot (right-handed; left-handed checked later, see above) and shows three lines; the settings at GUI scale 4; the look picker in Hebrew; Light mode skips the word outline.
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 1.21.11 (fourth batch):**
  - Arabic words in the World layout show every letter, including the last one
  - lyrics without timing come out word by word in the World layout, and the last line clears
  - a very long word is shrunk to a slice of the view, and the other words stay visible
  - a wrapped Arabic line in the Lines layout fills row by row with the singing
  - Hebrew lines keep their reading order in the Lines and Arc layouts and on the Record card
  - the top bar shows "שלום world 5" as "world 5 שלום" and puts the Hebrew words of an English line in reading order; on a long Chinese line it follows a few characters at a time
  - a long Chinese line wraps into rows in the Arc layout and comes in a few characters at a time; Chinese and Japanese characters fade in one by one in the Lines layout; Thai and a 60-letter word wrap inside the line
  - settings rows with a long description put their buttons under the name at GUI scale 2, 3 and 4, with nothing overlapping
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 26.3 and 1.21.1 (fourth batch):** Arabic letters in the World layout and mixed Hebrew and English in the top bar, as above.
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 1.21.11 and 1.21.1 (fifth batch):** the top hat, propeller cap, flower crown, shades, headphones, straw cone and pumpkin sit outside an iron helmet and a carved pumpkin, and look as before on a bare head; the crown, horns and halo aren't oddly big with a helmet; an elytra doesn't change the hat; the antennae sway smoothly over a minute of frames.
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 1.21.11 (sixth batch):** in the World layout, "hello שלום," keeps its comma on the right of שלום, and a Hebrew line still puts it on the left; in the Lines layout, a line wrapped onto three rows fills row by row from each row's first word; plain English and Hebrew lines look as before.
- **Seen in game on Minecraft 1.21.11 (seventh batch):** in the top bar, "hello שלום, world" keeps the comma on the right of שלום and a Hebrew line keeps it on the left; Arabic letters stay joined, and the gaps around words with vowel marks are even.
- **Not seen in game yet:** seeking back inside the line being sung in the World layout (tests; in a short look nothing went wrong and jumps back to an earlier line cleared as they should, but a jump inside one line wasn't caught for sure); the lyrics, updater, saved-file and Spotify fixes (they have tests instead); the Windows, Mac and Linux music player fixes (tested on Windows and Mac by GitHub's build where possible); the Narrator (the test PC has no speech); lines that share a time (tests); and the song title at a portal, the Arc fade after switching back, lyrics turned off and on, and the album cover and colour tint after a quick skip (tried, but not clearly caught on screenshots).
